title: What meters do
description: An ammeter sits in the path and reads current. A voltmeter sits across two points and reads a difference.

blocks.md:
## Through versus across

An ammeter measures current, so it must sit in the path: the flow goes through it. A voltmeter measures a difference, so it sits across two points: it does not become the path. Swap those jobs and you tell a lie — or you short something.

This bites when you “put the voltage meter in the wire like the current meter.” Voltage is not a flow through a point. Current is not a height you read on one clip.

![Ammeter in series, voltmeter across](assets/meters.svg)

```text
A  in series   measures I  (through)
V  across      measures V  (difference)
```

A common mistake is treating V as something you read through a single wire. Place the meters, then match the words.

blocks.promptMd: Drop A on the meter that sits in the path. Drop V on the meter that sits across two points.
blocks.explainMd: A sits in the loop. V sits across two points. R is leftover.
